principles: One source of truth for dispatch identity and authority
Fail closed before generating any prompt
Compatibility must be explicit and testable
User-visible hints must be executable under the same schema
drivers: Cover every type and alias with table-driven tests

options.name: A: Add targeted conditionals and corrected hint text
cons: Does not satisfy the approved registry contract

options.name: B: Introduce a typed registry shared by all dispatch consumers
pros: Aliases and cardinality become enumerable and testable
Supports future roles without privilege inference

chosen: B: Introduce a typed registry shared by all dispatch consumers
rationale: The observed failures come from duplicated and implicit authority, so localized conditionals would only mask two instances. A shared typed registry directly enforces the approved Workstream C invariants and makes every compatibility path auditable.

preMortem.scenario: A valid legacy alias stops dispatching
preMortem.trigger: Registry omits test-intent or test-case-reviewer compatibility entry
preMortem.consequence: Existing workflows fail despite safer routing
preMortem.mitigation: Enumerate aliases explicitly and add table-driven compatibility cases for canonical and legacy names

preMortem.scenario: Unknown role still receives implementer prompt
preMortem.trigger: A consumer defaults before registry resolution
preMortem.consequence: Role can receive mutation and commit guidance
preMortem.mitigation: Resolve and validate the type at the dispatch entry before selecting cardinality, policy, or prompt builder; add negative prompt-content assertions

preMortem.trigger: Transition text constructs calls independently of registry cardinality
preMortem.consequence: Operators follow a suggested command that the handler rejects
preMortem.mitigation: Generate hint invocation shape from registry metadata and execute every emitted example in smoke tests

preMortem.trigger: Role-class migration changes finding or pass classification semantics
preMortem.consequence: Implementer evidence may count as independent reviewer proof
preMortem.mitigation: Keep permission metadata explicit, update process-fact contract, and test denied command classes for both reviewer and implementer roles
